title: Jule – rules
sub: One die, paper and pen: roll the numbers 1 to 6 in order and then strike them off again from 6 to 1. The quiet version, Silent Jule, is the same – but whoever makes a sound starts again.

seo.rulesT: Jule Dice Game Rules – also Silent Jule
seo.rulesD: How to play Jule: roll 1 to 6 in order with one die, then back from 6 to 1. Setup, a sample round, the way back, scoring, Silent Jule, variants and FAQ.

goal: The goal: be the first to roll every number from 1 to 6 in the right order – and then all the way back from 6 to 1.

info.label: Fact sheet
info.gearAlt: One die, a sheet of paper and a pen
info.intro: Jule is pure luck and takes one minute to explain – perfect for kids, for waiting in the hostel kitchen and for anyone who just wants to roll dice. It shows up in almost every German games compendium, usually together with its sneaky sister, Silent Jule.

setupLead: Jule works with any number of players from two upwards. All you need:
setup1: One die – a dice cup is nice but not required.
setup2: Paper and a pen for each player, or one sheet with a column for every name.
setup3: A start player: everyone rolls once, the highest number begins. After that the die goes round clockwise.
setupP: Everyone writes their name at the top of their sheet. Below it you will note the numbers you have reached, one under the other.
turnLead: Every player always needs exactly one number: at the start the 1, then the 2, the 3 and so on up to the 6.
s2p: If you rolled the number you need, write it down. Next time you need the next one: after the 1 the 2, after the 2 the 3.
s3p: Any other number counts for nothing – not even a higher one. Either way, the die goes to your left-hand neighbour.
exAlt: Example round: Anna needs a 3 and rolls a 3, Ben needs a 1 and rolls a 4, Cem needs a 5 and rolls a 5, Anna needs a 4 and rolls a 2.
exP: Anna and Cem each get one step further. Ben is still waiting for his first 1, and Anna's 2 in the next round doesn't help her because she now needs the 4.
backLead: Once you have all six numbers on your sheet, you turn round. Now you need the numbers in falling order – first the 6, then the 5, all the way down to the 1 – and strike each one off as soon as you roll it.
sheetAlt: Anna's sheet: 1 to 6 written down on the way there. On the way back the 6 and the 5 are already struck off, she now needs the 4.
sheetNote: Anna has struck off the 6 and the 5 – next she needs the 4.
backP: Your 6 at the top of the way there doesn't count twice: to start the way back you have to roll another 6.
winLead: Whoever strikes off their 1 first has made it there and back and wins the round. The others stop at once.
scoreP: If you play several rounds, give the losers penalty points:
score1: Each loser adds up the numbers they still need – those not yet written down on the way there plus those not yet struck off on the way back. Whoever is still waiting for their first 1 gets the most.
score2: After a few rounds the player with the fewest penalty points wins. In old games compendiums the losers pay the winner one cent per point instead.
silentLead: Silent Jule is played exactly like Jule, with one extra rule: nobody may make a sound.
silent1: No talking, laughing, humming, groaning or cheering – from the first roll to the last.
silent2: Whoever makes a sound loses everything on their sheet and starts again at the 1.
silent3: Gestures, grimaces and pointing are allowed. Trying to make the others laugh is very much part of the game.
silentP: Silent Jule is a favourite with parents and grandparents whenever the room gets too loud – and it turns a simple luck game into a real test of nerves.
varLead: Agree on the rules before the first roll. Common house rules:
var1: Three rolls: everyone gets up to three rolls per turn and stops at the first hit. Makes the game much faster with many players.
var2: Keep rolling: after a hit you may roll again straight away, as long as you keep hitting.
var3: Just there: no way back – whoever writes down the 6 first wins. Good for small children.
var4: Gentle silence: in Silent Jule a sound only costs you your last number instead of the whole sheet.
var5: Two dice, 2 to 12: roll two dice and count their sum. You need 2, 3, 4 … up to 12 and back. Takes longer – the 2 and the 12 are rare.
var6: Lagging player starts: whoever is furthest behind at the end of a round starts the next one, giving them a slight head start.
faq1q: Does a higher number count, for example a 5 when I need a 3?
faq1a: No. Only exactly the number you need counts. Everything else is a miss and the die moves on.
faq2q: How long does a game take?
faq2a: On average you need six rolls for each number, so with twelve numbers it is around 70 rolls per player. With four players that is about 15 minutes. With many players, use the three-roll variant.
faq3q: Do I need the 6 again to start the way back?
faq3a: Yes. The 6 that completes the way there is written down, then you have to roll another 6 to strike it off – see The way back.
faq4q: What counts as a sound in Silent Jule?
faq4a: Anything you can hear: words, laughing, coughing on purpose, humming. Agree beforehand whether sneezing counts – most groups are lenient there.
faq5a: Nobody really knows – Jule is simply a German girl's name. In some regions the dice game Schocken is also called Jule, so check which game your group means.
faq6a: Yes, as a challenge: count how many rolls you need to get there and back, and try to beat your record.
